newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 17.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a positive result which extends a series of encouraging performances by the Australian stockmarket, the All Ordinaries Index rose 24.7 points to finish at 2406.4, driven by a wave of confidence on Wall Street as strong United States inflation figures allayed fears of an imminent rise in interest rates. Page 1.

In findings which contrast with a claim from the Australian Stock Exchange that every one of the country's top 150 companies had complied with its new listing rules, a study by the Australian Investment Managers' Association has found that just 10 per cent of Australia's top 100 listed companies had an adequate understanding of their obligations to comply with the ASX's regulation on corporate governance ethics. Page 1.

Under a deal expected to boost the value of Smorgon Steel to around A$1 billion, the company has paid A$140 million for Welded Mesh, the structural materials division of Leighton Holdings Ltd, fuelling rumours the Smorgon family is preparing another attempt to sell its business. Page 19.

South-American-owned Bunge International seems certain to gain control of Defiance Mills after yesterday lifting its bid from A$1.70-a-share to A$1.95-a-share and finalising a deal which saw Defiance Mill's major shareholder, the O'Brien family, sell out of the flour miller after being offered an additional A$6 million. Page 19.

Speaking at the Australian Petroleum Production and Exploration Association conference yesterday, Ampol managing director Ian Blackburne criticised the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission for its intervention in the petroleum refining industry, saying it would cause the closure of several of the country's oil refineries and would force the departure of at least one of Australia's major players. Page 19.

The managing director of Metal Manufacturers Ltd, Glenn Dudley, announced yesterday that the group had scored a new Asian joint venture with US-based Corning Inc, but warned that an increase in competition and reduced domestic demand for the company's core cable products would result in lower first-half earnings in 1996-97. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

According to a study commissioned by the Australian Investment Managers Association, which represents 63 of the country's largest fund managers, up to 90 per cent of Australia's top 100 listed firms fall short of international best practice in disclosure of their corporate governance practices and policies. Page 17.

Perth-based Formulab Neuronetics Corp has encountered another hurdle, with Shaw Stockbroking, which has handled the bulk of trade in FNC since its re-listing in late 1995, reassessing its recommendation of the technology group flowing its failure to list on the New York Stock Exchange's Nasdaq index. Page 17.

Defiance Holdings Ltd, which held a 38.7 per cent stake in family milling and baking group Defiance Mills Ltd, yesterday accepted a revised unconditional offer from Brazilian food conglomerate Bunge International, taking Bunge to ownership of 17.9 million ordinary shares or 43.2 per cent of the company. Page 17.

Woodside Petroleum Ltd confirmed yesterday the sale of three cargoes of 175,000 cubic metres of liquefied natural gas to customers in the United States - the first such sale to the US since a temporary downturn in demand from key Japanese customers. The sale has opened up a potentially profitable new market for the partners in the A$12 billion North West Shelf gas project. Page 19.

More than 350 workers at BHP's lucrative Escondida copper-gold mine have threatened to strike over the latest remuneration package offered by mine operator Minera Escondida, of which BHP and RTZ-CRA are the major shareholders. The workers voted yesterday on whether to accept the deal and the result will be released early today. Page 19.

After posting a 2.3 per cent increase in third-quarter profit yesterday to A$31.8 million on gold sales of 364,081 ounces, compared with 366,429 ounces previously, Normandy Mining Ltd is on course to report an annual net profit of about A$115 million, with gold production expected to be boosted by the Vera Nancy mine in Queensland. Page 19
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

While the Federal Government needs economic growth for the six months to June 30 to hit an annualised rate of more than six per cent to meet its forecast of 3.5 per cent growth for 1996-97, a report released yesterday by the United Nations-affiliated Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific said Australia would reach an average growth rate of 2.9 per cent up to 2000, the lowest in the region. Page 27.

Tomorrow will see the debut of Diamond Rose - a diamond explorer controlled by Pnina Feldman, the sister of mining magnate Joe Gutnick - on the Australian Stock Exchange. The company plans to spend the A$10 million raised through its float on exploring prospective ground in Western Australia and New South Wales. Page 27.

In comments which follow a round of intense meetings between Australia's petrol refiners and the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, Ampol Petroleum managing director Ian Blackburne said yesterday the Commission had adopted a position that would see the demise of the country's A$25 billion petroleum refining industry. Page 27.

Qantas Airways, which is currently on an aggressive cost-cutting regime, is believed to have joined the Speedrail consortium that is competing against three other groups to acquire the rights to build and operate a high-speed train between Sydney and Canbrra. Speedrail has proposed a privately funded and operated service, using TGV trains on a new track. Page 27.

According to a study by the Australian Investment Managers' Association which focused on the top 100 listed Australian companies and was carried out by Corporate Governance International, the nation's companies fall well short of international best practice when it comes to the quality and level of disclosure about their handling of corporate governance. Page 29.

In a strong result which Normandy Mining executive chairman Robert de Crespigny predicted would set the company up for a solid fourth quarter, Australia's largest goldminer yesterday posted a third quarter net profit of A$31.8 million, 2.3 per cent higher than the December quarter. Page 29.
THE AGE

The Federal Government has appointed BZW Australia's corporate advisory group as its business advisor for the upcoming one-third sale of Telstra. Federal Finance Minister John Fahey also announced the Melbourne office of Freehill, Hollingdale and Page had secured the role of domestic legal advisor to the Federal Government on the Telstra sale. Page B1.

Coca- Cola Amatil announced yesterday that it plans to continue with its A$4.1 billion deal with San Miguel Corp of the Philippines, despite protests from 48 per cent of San Miguel's shareholders that the deal be renegotiated. Under the agreement, San Miuel Corp will receive 25 per cent of CCA in exchange for the local Coke franchise, Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc. Page B1.

A study by the Australian Investment Managers Association reveals that Australia lags behind international standards for disclosing corporate governance practice. Companies it praised for having good corporate government included: North, CSR, Goodman Fieder, CSL and Lend Lease. Companies criticised for poor disclosure were Brambles, Santos and Brickworks. Page B1.

A public row has erupted between two leading tobacco companies with Henry Goldberg, chief executive of Philip Morris Australia, and Stuart Watterton of W.D. & H.O. Wills, each publicly accusing the other of responsibility for the latest price rises in cigarettes. Page B1.

The North-West Shelf gas project has sold three cargoes of gas worth approximately A$40 million to the Cabot group in Boston in the United States. It is the group's first sale in the United States market. The sale was made in response to the decision by Japanese customers to take 125 cargoes of gas this year instead of the usual 130. Page B3.

Diamond explorer company Diamond Rose will tomorrow make its debut on the Australian Stock Exchange following a float which has already raised A$10 million for exploration purposes in Western Australia and New South Wales. The company is headed by Pnina Feldman, sister of mining magnate Joe Gutnick. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
